info.title: Koshee Protect
info.summary: API for interacting with Koshee Protect servers
info.description:
Provides an API for interacting with Koshee Protect servers

## Features

* Read output of detect and interact with results of models on cameras over different date runs
* Read output of track manager and interact with results of track ids
* Upload base tracks to use in track manager runs
* Upload videos to use in detect runs
* Request model runs against single images
* Modify detect and track configurations
* Run detect and track configurations

post.description:
**Logs into the system**

Creates an access token and a refresh token if username and password
are authenticated.

- **form_data**: the user request form.

**Logs into the system via Google**

Validates a Google ID token and returns an internal access token and
refresh token.

- **request**: body containing the Google ID token from the client.

**Refreshes an access token**

Exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access token and a new refresh
token. The presented refresh token stops working (rotation) and the
session is extended by the refresh token lifetime (sliding window).
Does not require an access token, so it works after the access token
has expired.

- **request**: body containing the refresh token.

**Logs out**

Revokes the session that owns the refresh token. If **all_sessions** is
true, revokes every session for that user (logout on all devices).
Always succeeds, even if the token is unknown or already revoked.
Access tokens already issued remain valid until they expire.

- **request**: body containing the refresh token and all_sessions flag.

post.description:
**Gets similar images from a source image_path**   
This function has a lot of settings and overrides. Here is a list of some of
the more confusing ones that might not be clear from examples.
 
category: can be "any person", "any vehicle", "any weapon", "any bag"   
config_name: the config to target similarity search into   
date_folder: the config replay folder to search into (exclusive with event_name)   
distance_filter: the max distance of a candidate in feet   
event_name: the config event folder to search into (exclusive with date_folder)   
event_type: can be "regularities", "keyframes", "warnings", or "anomalies"   
gps: the gps (lat, lon) that should be center of the distance filter   
image_path: image path on server, can be local to image search paths   
max_images: the maximum number of images to return, sorted by similarity   
time_filter: a time distance which can be expressed in a human readable form such as "12m" for 12 minutes and "1h 20m" for 1 hour and 20 minutes

post.description:
**Overrides current user preferences with approved changes**. Note that not all
  user preferences can be overridden. To see a list of preferences that are likely
  to be allowed, call this method with a GET to see a filtered list of preferences.
  These preferences can affect Protect's detect and track manager processes, as
  well as the GUI functionality. It is recommended that interoperable and
  accessibility settings such as font sizes are kept consistent for users of
  external applications. Consequently, it is very likely that font sizes should
  be consistent in preferences as applied to the Protect GUI as well as external
  web or other applications.

  Each preference key is optional. You can even send an empty dictionary. The
  following preferences are possible:

  * fonts.labels.family: the font family (Roboto, Arial, Verdana, Helvetica)
  * fonts.labels.size: the font size (>6)
  * fonts.buttons.family: the font family (Roboto, Arial, Verdana, Helvetica)
  * fonts.buttons.size: the font size (>6)
  * fonts.dropdowns.family: the font family (Roboto, Arial, Verdana, Helvetica)
  * fonts.dropdowns.size: the font size (>6)
  * original_image_width: the pixel width to resize images to (should be close to model network width)
  * resize_originals_policy: when to resize originals. "None", "Always", "Live Camera Only", "Video File Only"
  * replay.event_min_type: default playback level. "regularities", "keyframes", "anomalies"
  * model_policy: models that will show up in list. "Nvidia", "AMD", "Intel", "Any"
  * replay_camera_width: pixel width of camera frames in Replay tab
  * replay_camera_height: pixel height of camera frames in Replay tab (may be discarded to prefer aspect ratio)
  * replay_controls_size: pixel width/height of control buttons like play, stop, etc.
  * replay_show_labels: boolean where true means to display captions on frames during playback
  * replay_scheduler_policy: replays allocate threads that can prioritize fairness or events. "Fair", "Priority"
  * replay_has_keyframes_priority: priority of cameras that have keyframes in Priority scheduler policy
  * replay_has_anomalies_priority: priority of cameras that have anomalies in Priority scheduler policy
  * replay_has_unvisited_anomalies_priority: priority of cameras that have unvisited anomalies in Priority scheduler policy
  * replay_scheduler_threads: number of threads to set for replay tab camera playback (>=1)
  * replay_blur_detector: blur detector (e.g., detect_person) to use during camera replay (unused atm)
  * track_blur_detector: blur detector (e.g., detect_person) to use during track tab copy originals function
  * replay_show_cam_labels: boolean where true means to display camera labels on cameras
  * similarity_model_size: how detailed to be in track similarity scoring ("Normal", "Detailed")
